text:
Recent evidence cautions against treating sampled ranking as a proxy for full-catalog ranking. RecSys 2025’s [On the Reliability of Sampling Strategies](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) separates resolution, fidelity, robustness to exposure bias, and recovery of preference-based rankings; sampler reliability depends on sparsity, exposure, and sample size. A [2024 sequential-recommendation study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) finds random negative sampling reinforces popularity bias and favors head items. Keep pinned 99-negative validation HR@10 as the selection criterion; report full-catalog unseen-item ranking and popularity-matched/text-similar candidate results as separate diagnostics.

Training margins are hypotheses about generalization, not established evidence of held-out ranking quality. A [2024 theoretical analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.07770) connects recommendation losses to ranking bounds and shows single-negative BPR/CCE equivalence, but does not establish that training margins predict failures on difficult held-out candidates. For this GRU4Rec task, measure whether margin bins predict validation misses within training-frequency and history-length slices. Construct text similarity only from available titles/descriptions; unobserved items can be relevant, so difficult negatives are not verified dislikes. True exposure-normalized errors are unavailable without exposure logs; interaction frequency is only a labeled proxy.

Recommended controlled protocol: paired user-level bootstrap intervals, resampling users within each category and recomputing the four-category macro mean; report paired improvement intervals and slice counts. The 2025 reliability study uses 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Change one factor at a time—negative sampling, loss, or recurrent memory—while fixing seeds, splits, training budget, and evaluator. Each variant must retain one independently trained GRU4Rec model per category. Treat diagnostic associations as exploratory; repeated validation-driven search weakens nominal confidence-interval interpretation.
